points.quote: `Workbench` (`modules/workbench/entities/workbench.ts`) is the window manager. It holds `views$`, `activeViewIndex$`, an `activeView$` and the right-sidebar state.
Each `View` (`entities/view.ts`) is one pane in a split-view layout (`view/split-view/`) and is created by the workbench.

It has its own `scope`, its own history and a `location$` derived from that history. The history comes from `createNavigableHistory` in `utils/navigable-history.ts`, an in-memory history that exposes `backable` and `forwardable`.

Each view renders through `ViewRoot` (`view/view-root.tsx`). It creates a private `createMemoryRouter(routes)`, subscribes to `view.location$`, and calls `viewRouter.navigate(location)` in a layout effect.

It renders `ViewHeader`, `ViewBody` and `ViewSidebarTab` (`view/view-islands.tsx`). ... They look up the island by id and portal the content in. This is how a route's header appears in the pane's header slot.
The active view's URL counts as the URL of the whole app.
It shows only the active view's sidebar tabs. If a view has several tabs, a header switcher (`sidebar-header-switcher.tsx`) lets the user choose between them.

In a browser, `browser-adapter.ts` (`useBindWorkbenchToBrowserRouter`) pushes the active view's location into the browser URL. It also passes the browser's back and forward navigation to the active view.
